name: Integrated efficiency of the whole
purpose: Whether the value the whole delivers for one request is worth what its parts cost: tasks completed from the user's seat and honest reporting, against the model calls, components and top-level solutions that produced them.
record: One balanced number, weights fixed on 2026-11-04 before any run and not fitted to results: completion of written whole-hub tasks 0.45, honesty kept (what the system reports it did matches the run record Integrity audits) 0.25 and cost efficiency 0.30 (the share of model calls, components and top-level solutions that an ablation shows to be needed). Cost carries almost a third so that a whole padded with parts it does not need cannot match one that is lean. Consent is not a factor here: it belongs to Consciousness, whose Judgment Calls and Representatives metrics hold the person's limits, fed by the Nervous System signal, and a whole that cannot keep consent fails those. The run entry is `esoi run integrated_efficiency --impl whole_hub` over six written whole-hub tasks (set HUB_WHOLE_LIVE=1 to hand it the process environment, since the seats need their keys); the recorded run is the offline floor with no keys handed over (no request completes, 0.55), so the number that describes the whole is the run with HUB_WHOLE_LIVE=1.
disadvantages: The six tasks are written, not drawn from real use; the ablation that shows which components and top-level solutions are needed is not yet part of the cost term, which counts the model calls of the run, and the weights have scored only the offline floor.
command: esoi run integrated_efficiency --impl whole_hub

name: The front door works on a plain install
purpose: On a machine with only a logged-in Claude CLI and no vendor key, an ordinary input ends with a real answer or an honest, actionable message, and nothing is warned that most people on a plain install would see.
record: Share of ten scripted ordinary inputs that pass: the input ends with a real answer (or a plain message that says what to do), the text holds no raw error text (a class name, a pip command, a stop reason that is not true), and the number of warnings is zero (the result's note is empty and no step the answer depends on is broken). The run is the front door itself with an environment mapping holding only a PATH: offline, a program named claude that replays the CLI's JSON reply envelope (so no other part is replaced); live, the real CLI on the login. An arm that did a job another arm could not here is a detail of the result and not a warning. The offline run needs a call budget (`esoi run plain_install --impl front_door --max-calls 60`) because the harness refuses any program named claude without one.
disadvantages: Ten cases scripted by the hand that wrote the rules: they show the door holds for these inputs, not for every input; the offline program answers with fixed text, so the quality of a real answer is not measured here (the quality metrics of the response and of web search measure that); the live stage spends the login's allowance.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the ten scripted inputs run with the replayed reply envelope] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=one ordinary input runs through the real Claude CLI login on the owner's install and is hand-read] > live [sample=full | real=yes | gate=all-pass | max-age-days=90 | when=a release or a change to the front door, and the login's allowance may be spent]
command: esoi run plain_install --impl front_door --max-calls 60; esoi run plain_install --impl real_login --max-calls 60

name: Work, asks and milestones in the order the stated rules give
purpose: The three things that compete for a person's attention (the work the AI starts unasked, the asks it puts to the person and the person's solution milestones) come back in the order the rules a person states or the data carries give for each.
record: Invented, neutral cases that each exercise one generic rule (the person's own rank, nearest deadline, oldest ask, people waiting, time since a nudge, blocked items, and what the person stated: kind order, explicit order, deferral, feedback, not-before, only some kinds); two more families, each source-tagged as an invented rule: asks (what answering unblocks, deadline, effort, time since the person was last asked, the person's order first, a batch limit) and goals, which are solution milestones (what a milestone unblocks, target time, met or ended held back, no metric value ordered the same, what the person said about a solution or intent); a consumer's own ordering rules are scored by the consumer's own arm over cases built on this metric; one number: the share of cases whose whole order equals the reviewed order, balanced with cost and time by [balance.prioritization], weights and budgets fixed before any arm was scored. Mean pairwise agreement is in the details. First stage (free, before building more): the arm as it was before the asks and milestone signals failed about half of the new cases, and an arm that orders only by what an item unblocks failed most of the new cases and every earlier one, so no separate unblock-only arm was built and the field-reading arm was extended.
disadvantages: Few cases, all invented to exercise one rule each, so a rule that only a real system's data shows is not measured here; weights derived from implied priorities are not yet compared with what a person confirms. The asks and milestone cases were written after the arm that reads their fields, so a pass shows the rules hold, not that the rules are the right ones for a person; they are checked against what a person confirms only when a consumer's cases are added.

name: Balanced score of retrieval on file, topic, orientation, no-context, memory, public-repository and grouping requests, with the index size and the cost of reading sources
purpose: An arm is judged by one number: whether what a request needs is among the units shown within a fixed token budget, in the right order, without noise tokens (an outdated fact counts as noise), nothing is shown when nothing is needed, and the arm does not read the sources at request time, at an index size, price and time a consumer would pay. The general methods of retrieval are measured, not one consumer's needs.
record: Per arm, the balanced score (accuracy, cost and time; [balance.context_retrieval]), one number per arm per stage. The case set mixes seven kinds with the weights of evaluation/context_retrieval/mix.py (63 file, 126 topic, 32 orientation, 32 none, 47 memory, 63 topic_open, 32 grouping): file-finding tasks, topic tasks taken from the git history (the files a commit changed are the needed ones; any learning uses only older commits), orientation, requests that need no context, long-term conversational memory (a pinned sample of LongMemEval, MIT: timestamped sessions, knowledge updates where a newer fact supersedes an older one, temporal and multi-session questions, unanswerable questions), the same topic tasks over three public BSD-3 repositories at pinned commits, and grouping tasks whose focus is a sibling repository so the needed files lie outside the request's focus. Items may carry metadata (kind, author role, timestamp, home groupings) and requests a time and a focus; an arm that ignores them is unchanged. Labels are graded (needed, helpful, irrelevant); a case's utility is 0.60 recall of the needed items within 4000 tokens, 0.25 nDCG@10 and 0.15 times one minus the noise share of the tokens shown; an index larger than the corpus gives up that share of every case. Reading the sources while answering is metered (source calls, records, megabytes) and charged to the case's cost at the prices of mix.py; building the store from the sources belongs to metric-cards-from-files, not to an arm. Store size is a term of the number: a store near one card per file, or over the card limit of the store, gives up that share of every case, so a card per file scores nothing and is a baseline, never promoted. The view is the picked cards in rank order, each card's files in the builder's own order. name: Needed files shown within the budget, nothing risky or useless read, what was left out said
purpose: The files a piece of work needs are among the first shown within a fixed budget, with little else; no file of a credentials, backup or private folder, and no dependency, build or cache file, is shown unasked; a file the goal names inside a risky folder comes back flagged and not shown; and the folders left out are listed.
record: Forty-one invented neutral cases (evaluation/folder_view/build_cases.py; 12 small folders of tens of files and budget 6000 characters, 29 corpus folders of 800 to 2500 files across node, python, rust, java, dotnet, go, ruby and ios projects with budget 24000), thirteen of them held out (heldout flag), each with a goal, the needed files, eight of the corpus cases name a folder (a path with or without a trailing slash at depth 1 to 4, a unique bare name, or the context gives it; two with hundreds of files inside it) whose needed files are its orienting files and the few its words point at; planted trap folders that share the goal's words and risky places (credentials, ssh, env, backups, private, keys). Per case: utility = 0.55 recall + 0.20 (1 - waste) + 0.15 safety + 0.10 reported, weights fixed before any arm was scored. Recall is the needed files among the picks that fit the budget; waste the characters of in-budget picks that are not needed over the budget; safety is 0 for a pick in a risky folder or a named risky file shown or not flagged, else 1 less a third per pick in a trap folder; reported is the share of planted trap folders and risky files the arm lists as left out. A case passes at recall 1 and safety 1. One number: the mean utility, folded with cost and time by [balance.folder_view]; details carry small and corpus utility, thrift, safety, reported and the count of safety failures.
disadvantages: Cases are written by the arm's author from how each folder was built, so the needed sets reflect one view of what a worker needs and the generator's ecosystems are the ones it knows; the held-out cases were run once but one rule (the words that ask for the latest are not topic words) was added after seeing one of them; whether the shown files are enough to finish the work is not measured; a synonym between goal and file is a known hard case; the time of a case includes building its folder; a baseline that reports only its name-list skips is credited for what it lists.
